Pre-cycle hints for v1.15 theme pick (recorded 2026-05-05 when v1.14 trimmed its candidate list to theme E + #84).

USER SIGNAL — SEARCH IS HIGH-LEVERAGE:
At v1.14 trim time, user agreed to defer theme B (search/discoverability — #13 fzf, #43 boolean operators) to v1.15 backlog but explicitly flagged regret: search has token-efficiency upside, not just feature value. The framing matters — search isn't a "nice to have" feature category for codexCLI; bad discoverability forces agents to bootstrap with codex_context (high token cost) instead of targeted codex_get (low cost). A B-themed v1.15 would close that gap and pair naturally with v1.14's theme E (guardrails make the store cleaner; search makes the cleaner store cheaper to navigate).

HOW TO APPLY:
- When Phase 2 of v1.15 picks a theme, weight B above its surface signal in the dataset. The user already endorsed it once.
- Don't auto-pick B — Phase 1 dataset still gates the decision. But if signal is ambiguous between two themes, B wins the tiebreak.
- If a different theme dominates the v1.15 dataset clearly (e.g. distribution because npx adoption surge, or polish because perf complaints), follow the data — this hint isn't an override, it's a tiebreaker.

REMAINING v1.14-TRIMMED CANDIDATES (in v1.15 backlog as unmilestoned):
- A (metadata): #42 git-aware freshness, #45 entry attribution
- B (search): #13 fzf, #43 boolean operators ← user-flagged
- C (distribution): #6 fish/PowerShell, #49 Windows, #50 npx, #51 IDE extensions
- D (polish/perf): #44 richer types, #47 ccli diff, #48 perf benchmarks

CAVEAT:
This is N=1 input from one trim conversation. Track whether v1.15 dataset agrees. If post-v1.15 the user re-evaluates and says "search wasn't actually the win I thought," update or remove this entry.
